html:
Duklja was a medieval South Slav state on the coast and hills of today's Montenegro, named after the Roman town of Doclea near Podgorica. It broke free of Byzantine rule in the 1040s under Prince Stefan Vojislav, a generation after the fall of Tsar Samuel's empire.

His son Mihailo won a crown from Pope Gregory VII in 1077, making Duklja a kingdom. Under King Bodin it ruled over Serbian lands inland and Bosnia for a time. Its churches looked to Rome and Constantinople alike. By the late 1100s it was taken into the Serbia of Stefan Nemanja and became known as Zeta. Montenegrins see Duklja as the first state of their own, and its history was written in the Chronicle of the Priest of Duklja.
